title: Global Catastrophic Risks
pitch: An early scholarly survey of risks that could cripple human civilisation, from asteroids and pandemics to nuclear war, nanotechnology and AI.

chapters.g: Why such risks are neglected and how cognitive biases distort our judgment about them.
Super volcanoes, asteroids and other natural threats, and how often they happen.
Climate change, pandemics and other side effects of human activity.
Nuclear war, nuclear and biological terrorism, and totalitarian states.
Yudkowsky argues AI could be a positive or negative factor and that friendliness must be designed in.
Speculative risks from new technology and big experiments.

ideas: Global catastrophic risks deserve far more study than they get.
Our biases make us bad at judging rare disasters.
Human made risks may outweigh natural ones.
AI could be among the biggest factors, for good or ill.

args.a: Catastrophic risks are neglected compared with their stakes.
args.c: Others argue resources should go to known present problems.

args.a: AI deserves a place on the list.
args.c: In 2008 this was rare. Since then AI risk has moved into mainstream statements and summits.

questions: Which risk on the list do you think is most neglected?
How do biases distort how you think about rare events?
